source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּימֵי֙ אַמְרָפֶ֣ל מֶֽלֶךְ־שִׁנְעָ֔ר אַרְי֖וֹךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶלָּסָ֑ר כְּדָרְלָעֹ֨מֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֵילָ֔ם וְתִדְעָ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ גּוֹיִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim,

en.L: And it happened in the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim,
en.B: In the days when Amraphel was king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam and Tidal king of Goyim,
en.R: At that time there were four kings: Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam and Tidal king of Goyim.

decisions.choice: four kings from the east: rulers not identified with certainty
decisions.reason: Shinar is Babylonia and Elam lay east of it. The kings themselves have not been identified with known rulers. Goyim means "nations", perhaps a coalition of peoples. The chapter reads like an old record of war, unlike the stories around it.

source.text: עָשׂ֣וּ מִלְחָמָ֗ה אֶת־בֶּ֨רַע֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ סְדֹ֔ם וְאֶת־בִּרְשַׁ֖ע מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמֹרָ֑ה שִׁנְאָ֣ב׀מֶ֣לֶךְ אַדְמָ֗ה וְשֶׁמְאֵ֨בֶר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ צְבוֹיִ֔יםוּמֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּ֖לַע הִיא־צֹֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: they made war with Bera king of Sodom and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and [the] king of Bela, that [is] Zoar.

en.L: that they made war with Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, that [is], Zoar.
en.B: these kings went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar).
en.R: They went to war against five kings: Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela, which is also called Zoar.

decisions.choice: Zeboiim: the reading of the Masoretic margin
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew and the Masoretes' marginal reading spell the name slightly differently; the marginal reading is followed, as usual (also in verse 8).

decisions.choice: Bela, that is Zoar: an old name explained
decisions.reason: The narrator gives the later name for readers. Zoar is the town Lot later flees to (19:22).

source.text: כָּל־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ חָֽבְר֔וּ אֶל־עֵ֖מֶק הַשִּׂדִּ֑ים ה֖וּא יָ֥ם הַמֶּֽלַח׃

records.literal_gloss: All these joined together at [the] valley of Siddim, that [is the] Salt Sea.

en.L: All these joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, that [is], the Salt Sea.
en.B: All these kings joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, where the Dead Sea is now.
en.R: These five kings brought their armies together in the Valley of Siddim, the place now called the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the Salt Sea: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The Salt Sea is the Dead Sea. The note may mean that the valley later lay under the sea's southern waters, or simply that it was by the sea.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern name; Literal keeps "Salt Sea".

source.text: שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה עָבְד֖וּ אֶת־כְּדָרְלָעֹ֑מֶר וּשְׁלֹשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה מָרָֽדוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Twelve years they had served Kedorlaomer, and [in the] thirteenth year they rebelled.

en.L: Twelve years they had served Kedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
en.B: They had paid tribute to Kedorlaomer for twelve years, and in the thirteenth year they revolted.
en.R: For twelve years these five kings had been forced to serve Kedorlaomer. But in the thirteenth year they turned against him.

decisions.choice: served: were vassals of, paid tribute to
decisions.reason: To "serve" a king here means to be his vassal and pay him tribute.

source.text: וּבְאַרְבַּע֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה שָׁנָ֜ה בָּ֣א כְדָרְלָעֹ֗מֶר וְהַמְּלָכִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּכּ֤וּ אֶת־רְפָאִים֙ בְּעַשְׁתְּרֹ֣ת קַרְנַ֔יִם וְאֶת־הַזּוּזִ֖ים בְּהָ֑ם וְאֵת֙ הָֽאֵימִ֔ים בְּשָׁוֵ֖ה קִרְיָתָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And in [the] fourteenth year came Kedorlaomer and the kings who [were] with him, and they defeated [the] Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim and the Zuzites in Ham and the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim,

en.L: And in the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer and the kings who [were] with him came and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim,
en.B: In the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer came with his allied kings and crushed the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim
en.R: In the fourteenth year Kedorlaomer and the kings with him came and attacked. They defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham and the Emites in Shaveh-kiriathaim.

decisions.choice: Rephaites, Zuzites, Emites: ancient peoples east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: These were peoples remembered as tall and strong, living east of the Jordan before the Ammonites and Moabites (Deuteronomy 2:10-11, 20-21). The invaders sweep south along the King's Highway.

source.text: וְאֶת־הַחֹרִ֖י בְּהַרְרָ֣ם שֵׂעִ֑יר עַ֚ד אֵ֣יל פָּארָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: and the Horite[s] in their hill country of Seir as far as El-paran, which [is] by the wilderness.

en.L: and the Horites in their hill country of Seir, as far as El-paran, which [is] on the edge of the wilderness.
en.B: and the Horites in their hill country of Seir, as far as El-paran on the edge of the desert.
en.R: They also defeated the Horites in the hills of Seir, all the way to El-paran at the edge of the desert.

decisions.choice: the Horites of Seir: the people of Edom's hills before Esau
decisions.reason: Seir is the hill country later called Edom; the Horites lived there before Esau's descendants (36:20; Deuteronomy 2:12).

source.text: וַ֠יָּשֻׁבוּ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אֶל־עֵ֤ין מִשְׁפָּט֙ הִ֣וא קָדֵ֔שׁ וַיַּכּ֕וּ אֶֽת־כָּל־שְׂדֵ֖ה הָעֲמָלֵקִ֑י וְגַם֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בְּחַֽצְצֹ֥ן תָּמָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned back and came to En-mishpat, that [is] Kadesh, and defeated all [the] territory of the Amalekite[s] and also the Amorite[s] dwelling in Hazazon-tamar.

en.L: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat, that [is], Kadesh, and defeated all the territory of the Amalekites and also the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
en.B: Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat (that is, Kadesh), and they conquered the whole territory of the Amalekites, as well as the Amorites living in Hazazon-tamar.
en.R: Then they turned back north and came to En-mishpat, which is also called Kadesh. They conquered all the land of the Amalekites and the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.

decisions.choice: En-mishpat, that is Kadesh: an oasis in the south
decisions.reason: "Spring of judgment", later called Kadesh, is an oasis in the far south, where Israel camped in the wilderness (Numbers 20:1).

decisions.choice: the territory of the Amalekites: the region later held by them
decisions.reason: Amalek is a later people (36:12); the narrator names the region by the people his readers knew there.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ־סְדֹ֜ם וּמֶ֣לֶךְ עֲמֹרָ֗ה וּמֶ֤לֶךְ אַדְמָה֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ צְבוֹיִ֔ם וּמֶ֥לֶךְ בֶּ֖לַע הִוא־צֹ֑עַר וַיַּֽעַרְכ֤וּ אִתָּם֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה בְּעֵ֖מֶק הַשִּׂדִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] king of Sodom and [the] king of Gomorrah and [the] king of Admah and [the] king of Zeboiim and [the] king of Bela, that [is] Zoar, and they drew up for battle with them in [the] valley of Siddim,

en.L: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim and the king of Bela, that [is], Zoar, went out and drew up for battle against them in the Valley of Siddim,
en.B: Then the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim and Bela (that is, Zoar) marched out and took up battle positions in the Valley of Siddim
en.R: Then the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim and Bela marched out and got ready to fight in the Valley of Siddim.

source.text: אֵ֣ת כְּדָרְלָעֹ֜מֶר מֶ֣לֶךְ עֵילָ֗ם וְתִדְעָל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גּוֹיִ֔ם וְאַמְרָפֶל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ שִׁנְעָ֔ר וְאַרְי֖וֹךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶלָּסָ֑ר אַרְבָּעָ֥ה מְלָכִ֖ים אֶת־הַחֲמִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: with Kedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goyim, and Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar, four kings against the five.

en.L: against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goyim, Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar, four kings against five.
en.B: against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goyim, Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar: four kings against five.
en.R: They fought against Kedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goyim, Amraphel king of Shinar and Arioch king of Ellasar. It was four kings against five.

source.text: וְעֵ֣מֶק הַשִׂדִּ֗יםבֶּֽאֱרֹ֤ת בֶּאֱרֹת֙ חֵמָ֔ר וַיָּנֻ֛סוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־סְדֹ֥ם וַעֲמֹרָ֖ה וַיִּפְּלוּ־שָׁ֑מָּה וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִ֖ים הֶ֥רָה נָּֽסוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] valley of Siddim [was] pits, pits of bitumen; and fled [the] king of Sodom and Gomorrah and fell there, and those remaining fled to [the] hill country.

en.L: Now the Valley of Siddim [was full of] pit after pit of bitumen; and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, they fell into them, and those who remained fled to the hill country.
en.B: The Valley of Siddim was riddled with tar pits. As the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran, some of their men fell into them, and the survivors escaped into the hills.
en.R: The Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits. When the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ran away, some of their men fell into the pits. The others escaped to the hills.

decisions.choice: pits, pits: full of pits
decisions.reason: Repeating the word means there were pits everywhere.

decisions.choice: fell there: fell into the pits, or threw themselves into them
decisions.reason: "Fell" may mean they were trapped in the pits or that they hid in them. The king of Sodom is alive in verse 17, so not all who fell died.

source.text: וַ֠יִּקְחוּ אֶת־כָּל־רְכֻ֨שׁ סְדֹ֧ם וַעֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאֶת־כָּל־אָכְלָ֖ם וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took all [the] goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food and went.

en.L: And they took all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food, and went away.
en.B: The victors carried off everything from Sodom and Gomorrah, all their goods and food, and went on their way.
en.R: The four kings took everything from Sodom and Gomorrah, including all their food, and left.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֨וּ אֶת־ל֧וֹט וְאֶת־רְכֻשׁ֛וֹ בֶּן־אֲחִ֥י אַבְרָ֖ם וַיֵּלֵ֑כוּ וְה֥וּא יֹשֵׁ֖ב בִּסְדֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took Lot and his goods, [the] son of [the] brother of Abram, and went; and he was dwelling in Sodom.

en.L: They also took Lot, Abram's brother's son, and his goods, and went away; for he was living in Sodom.
en.B: Among the captives was Lot, Abram's nephew, who lived in Sodom; they took him and all he had.
en.R: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who was living in Sodom, and took everything he owned.

decisions.choice: he was living in Sodom: Lot's choice catches up with him
decisions.reason: Lot pitched his tent toward Sodom (13:12); now he lives in it, and he shares its fate in the war.

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאַבְרָ֣ם הָעִבְרִ֑י וְהוּא֩ שֹׁכֵ֨ן בְּאֵֽלֹנֵ֜י מַמְרֵ֣א הָאֱמֹרִ֗י אֲחִ֤י אֶשְׁכֹּל֙ וַאֲחִ֣י עָנֵ֔ר וְהֵ֖ם בַּעֲלֵ֥י בְרִית־אַבְרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And came the fugitive and told Abram the Hebrew; and he was dwelling at [the] great trees of Mamre the Amorite, [the] brother of Eshcol and [the] brother of Aner, and they [were] allies of Abram.

en.L: And one who had escaped came and told Abram the Hebrew. He was living by the great trees of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and of Aner; and these were allies of Abram.
en.B: Someone who escaped brought the news to Abram the Hebrew. Abram was camped by the great trees belonging to Mamre the Amorite, whose brothers were Eshcol and Aner; all three were bound by treaty to Abram.
en.R: One man escaped and came to tell Abram the Hebrew what had happened. Abram was living near the big trees that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's partners.

decisions.choice: Abram the Hebrew: the first use of the word
decisions.reason: This is the first time the word "Hebrew" appears. It is how others describe Abram's people (39:14; Exodus 2:6), and it is linked with the name Eber (10:21).

decisions.choice: allies of Abram: literally "masters of the covenant of Abram"
decisions.reason: They were bound to Abram by a treaty or agreement of alliance.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אַבְרָ֔ם כִּ֥י נִשְׁבָּ֖ה אָחִ֑יו וַיָּ֨רֶק אֶת־חֲנִיכָ֜יו יְלִידֵ֣י בֵית֗וֹ שְׁמֹנָ֤ה עָשָׂר֙ וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת וַיִּרְדֹּ֖ף עַד־דָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Abram that had been taken captive his brother, and he called out his trained men, born in his house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued as far as Dan.

en.L: When Abram heard that his kinsman had been taken captive, he called out his trained men, born in his household, 318 of them, and pursued as far as Dan.
en.B: As soon as Abram learned that his kinsman was a prisoner, he mustered the 318 trained men of his household, all born in his camp, and chased the enemy as far as Dan.
en.R: When Abram heard that his nephew had been captured, he gathered 318 trained fighting men who had been born into his household, and he chased the enemy as far north as Dan.

decisions.choice: his kinsman: literally "his brother"
decisions.reason: "Brother" is used broadly of a close relative; Lot is Abram's nephew.

decisions.choice: trained men born in his household: Abram's own fighting force
decisions.reason: The men were born to servants in Abram's household and trained to fight. That Abram had 318 of them shows how large and powerful his household was.

decisions.choice: Dan: the city in the far north, named by its later name
decisions.reason: The city was called Laish until the tribe of Dan took it (Judges 18:29); the narrator uses the name familiar to later readers.

source.text: וַיֵּחָלֵ֨ק עֲלֵיהֶ֧ם׀לַ֛יְלָה ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וַיַּכֵּ֑ם וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵם֙ עַד־חוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִשְּׂמֹ֖אל לְדַמָּֽשֶׂק׃

records.literal_gloss: And he divided himself against them by night, he and his servants, and struck them and pursued them as far as Hobah, which [is] north of Damascus.

en.L: And he divided his forces against them by night, he and his servants, and defeated them and pursued them as far as Hobah, which [is] north of Damascus.
en.B: He split his men into groups and fell on the enemy by night. He routed them and pursued them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
en.R: During the night Abram divided his men into groups and attacked. He won the battle and chased the enemy all the way to Hobah, north of Damascus.

decisions.choice: north of Damascus: literally "on the left of Damascus"
decisions.reason: Facing east, the left hand is north. The pursuit goes far beyond the land of Canaan.

source.text: וַיָּ֕שֶׁב אֵ֖ת כָּל־הָרְכֻ֑שׁ וְגַם֩ אֶת־ל֨וֹט אָחִ֤יו וּרְכֻשׁוֹ֙ הֵשִׁ֔יב וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְאֶת־הָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought back all the goods, and also Lot his kinsman and his goods he brought back, and also the women and the people.

en.L: And he brought back all the goods, and also brought back Lot his kinsman and his goods, and the women and the people too.
en.B: He got back all the plunder, and he brought back Lot his kinsman with his goods, as well as the women and the rest of the captives.
en.R: Abram brought back everything the enemy had taken. He also rescued his nephew Lot and all his things, and the women and the other people too.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ־סְדֹם֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒ אַחֲרֵ֣י שׁוּב֗וֹ מֵֽהַכּוֹת֙ אֶת־כְּדָרלָעֹ֔מֶרוְאֶת־הַמְּלָכִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ אֶל־עֵ֣מֶק שָׁוֵ֔ה ה֖וּא עֵ֥מֶק הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out [the] king of Sodom to meet him after his return from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings who [were] with him, to [the] valley of Shaveh, that [is the] King's Valley.

en.L: And after his return from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings who [were] with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him at the Valley of Shaveh, that [is], the King's Valley.
en.B: When Abram came back from his victory over Kedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, which is the King's Valley.
en.R: When Abram came back from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, also called the King's Valley.

decisions.choice: the King's Valley: near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: 2 Samuel 18:18 places the King's Valley near Jerusalem, which fits the meeting with the king of Salem (verse 18).

source.text: וּמַלְכִּי־צֶ֨דֶק֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ שָׁלֵ֔ם הוֹצִ֖יא לֶ֣חֶם וָיָ֑יִן וְה֥וּא כֹהֵ֖ן לְאֵ֥ל עֶלְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; and he [was] priest of God Most High.

en.L: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine; he [was] priest of God Most High.
en.B: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.
en.R: Then Melchizedek, the king of Salem, brought out bread and wine for Abram. Melchizedek was a priest who served God Most High.

decisions.choice: Melchizedek: "king of righteousness"
decisions.reason: The name means "my king is righteousness" or "king of righteousness". Hebrews 7:2 explains it so, and Salem as "peace".

decisions.choice: Salem: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Salem is an old name for Jerusalem (Psalm 76:2).

decisions.choice: God Most High (El Elyon): the high God, creator of all
decisions.reason: El was the common word for God; Elyon means "Most High". The title is used for the LORD in the Psalms (Psalm 7:17; 78:35). Abram identifies El Elyon with the LORD in verse 22.

decisions.choice: a priest-king: taken up in Psalm 110 and Hebrews
decisions.reason: Melchizedek appears without genealogy, both king and priest. Psalm 110:4 speaks of a king who is "a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek", and Hebrews 5-7 sees in him a picture of Christ.

source.text: וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֖הוּ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר בָּר֤וּךְ אַבְרָם֙ לְאֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן קֹנֵ֖ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he blessed him and said, blessed [be] Abram by God Most High, creator of heaven and earth;

en.L: And he blessed him and said, "Blessed [be] Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth;
en.B: He blessed Abram and said, "May Abram be blessed by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
en.R: He blessed Abram and said, "May God Most High, who made heaven and earth, bless Abram!

decisions.choice: Creator: maker or owner
decisions.reason: The word (qoneh) can mean maker or owner (it is related to Eve's "I have gotten", 4:1). Either way, heaven and earth belong to God Most High.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth: the whole of creation, as in 1:1
decisions.reason: The pair recalls 1:1. The God Melchizedek serves is the God of all creation.

source.text: וּבָרוּךְ֙ אֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן אֲשֶׁר־מִגֵּ֥ן צָרֶ֖יךָ בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ וַיִּתֶּן־ל֥וֹ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ר מִכֹּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and blessed [be] God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand. And he gave him a tenth of everything.

en.L: and blessed [be] God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand!" And he gave him a tenth of everything.
en.B: And blessed be God Most High, who has given your enemies into your power." Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
en.R: Praise God Most High, who helped you defeat your enemies!" Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything he had brought back.

decisions.choice: delivered: handed over
decisions.reason: The verb (miggen) sounds like the word for "shield" (magen) in 15:1. God gave the victory.

decisions.choice: he gave him a tenth: Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he gave him". The giver is Abram, giving a tithe of the spoils to the priest, as Hebrews 7:4 reads it.

decisions.choice: Abram gave
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the giver (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ־סְדֹ֖ם אֶל־אַבְרָ֑ם תֶּן־לִ֣י הַנֶּ֔פֶשׁ וְהָרְכֻ֖שׁ קַֽח־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] king of Sodom to Abram, give to me the persons, and the goods take for yourself.

en.L: And the king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself."
en.B: Then the king of Sodom said to Abram, "Let me have the people; you keep the goods."
en.R: The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me back my people, but you can keep everything else."

decisions.choice: give me the people, take the goods: a generous offer, by custom
decisions.reason: By custom the victor kept the spoils. The king of Sodom asks only for his people back. The contrast with Melchizedek, who gives and blesses, is pointed.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אַבְרָ֖ם אֶל־מֶ֣לֶךְ סְדֹ֑ם הֲרִימֹ֨תִי יָדִ֤י אֶל־יְהוָה֙ אֵ֣ל עֶלְי֔וֹן קֹנֵ֖ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abram to [the] king of Sodom, I raise my hand to YHWH, God Most High, creator of heaven and earth,

en.L: And Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
en.B: Abram answered the king of Sodom, "I have lifted my hand in an oath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth,
en.R: But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have made a solemn promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God Most High, who made heaven and earth.

decisions.choice: I raise my hand: I swear an oath
decisions.reason: Raising the hand was the gesture of taking an oath (Deuteronomy 32:40).

decisions.choice: the LORD, God Most High: Abram names Melchizedek's God as the LORD
decisions.reason: Abram uses Melchizedek's title and adds the name of his own God: the God Most High whom Melchizedek serves is the LORD.

decisions.choice: the LORD, as in the Hebrew text
alternatives: God Most High, without the LORD (Septuagint); the God Most High (Samaritan Pentateuch)
decisions.reason: The Septuagint and the Samaritan Pentateuch do not have the name the LORD here, matching Melchizedek's words in verses 18-20. The Hebrew text is followed.

source.text: אִם־מִחוּט֙ וְעַ֣ד שְׂרֽוֹךְ־נַ֔עַל וְאִם־אֶקַּ֖ח מִכָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לָ֑ךְ וְלֹ֣א תֹאמַ֔ר אֲנִ֖י הֶעֱשַׁ֥רְתִּי אֶת־אַבְרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: if from a thread to a sandal strap, if I will take from all that [is] yours, and not you will say, I have made Abram rich;

en.L: that I will not take a thread or a sandal strap or anything that is yours, so that you will not say, 'I have made Abram rich.'
en.B: that I will not keep a single thing of yours, not a thread, not a sandal strap. You will never be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'
en.R: that I will not take anything of yours, not even a piece of thread or a sandal strap. Then you will never be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'

decisions.choice: if I take ...: a form of oath meaning "I will certainly not take"
decisions.reason: An oath often began "if I do ..." with a curse understood ("may God punish me"). It means a strong "I will not".

decisions.choice: so that you will not say, I made Abram rich: Abram's wealth must come from God
decisions.reason: Abram refuses to owe anything to the king of Sodom. His wealth and blessing are to come from God Most High alone, unlike in Egypt (12:16).

source.text: בִּלְעָדַ֗י רַ֚ק אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽכְל֣וּ הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְחֵ֨לֶק֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלְכ֖וּ אִתִּ֑י עָנֵר֙ אֶשְׁכֹּ֣ל וּמַמְרֵ֔א הֵ֖ם יִקְח֥וּ חֶלְקָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: apart from me; only what the young men have eaten, and [the] share of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol and Mamre, let them take their share.

en.L: nothing for me except what the young men have eaten, and the share of the men who went with me, Aner, Eshcol and Mamre; let them take their share."
en.B: I will take nothing except what my young men have already eaten. But Aner, Eshcol and Mamre, who went with me, must have their share."
en.R: I will only accept the food my young men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol and Mamre, who went with me, should get their share."

decisions.choice: let them take their share: Abram does not bind his allies
decisions.reason: Abram's oath binds himself, not his allies; they receive the share due to them.
